```tsx
					label="29 Jul 2026"
					appearance="danger"
					isSpacious
					testId="date-label-dropdown-danger-spacious"
				/>
			</div>
			<div css={styles.row}>
				<DateLabelDropdownTrigger
					label="29 Jul 2026"
					appearance="neutral"
					hasIconBefore={false}
					testId="date-label-dropdown-no-icon"
				/>
				<DateLabelDropdownTrigger
					label="29 Jul 2026"
					appearance="neutral"
					hasIconBefore={false}
					isSpacious
					testId="date-label-dropdown-no-icon-spacious"
				/>
			</div>
			<div css={styles.row}>
				<Text>Selected:</Text>
				<DateLabelDropdownTrigger
					label="29 Jul 2026"
					appearance="neutral"
					isSelected
					testId="date-label-dropdown-neutral-selected"
				/>
				<DateLabelDropdownTrigger
					label="29 Jul 2026"
					appearance="warning"
					isSelected
					testId="date-label-dropdown-warning-selected"
				/>
				<DateLabelDropdownTrigger
					label="29 Jul 2026"
					appearance="danger"
					isSelected
					testId="date-label-dropdown-danger-selected"
				/>
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `appearance` | `DateLabelDropdownTriggerAppearance \| undefined` | Controls the visual style of the trigger. - `neutral` — default grey border style - `warning` — orange border, used for upcoming/near-due dates - `danger` — red border, used for overdue dates |
| `aria-controls` | `string \| undefined` | Identifies the popup element that this trigger controls. Should match the `id` of the popup content for screen readers. |
| `aria-expanded` | `boolean \| undefined` | Announces to assistive technology whether the popup is currently open. |
| `aria-haspopup` | `boolean \| "dialog" \| undefined` | Informs assistive technology that this element triggers a popup. |
| `aria-label` | `string \| undefined` | Defines a string value that labels the trigger element for assistive technology. If not provided, the `label` text is used as the accessible name. |
| `hasIconBefore` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true`, an icon is displayed before the label text. The icon shown depends on the `appearance`: - `neutral` → CalendarIcon - `warning` → ClockIcon - `danger` → WarningOutlineIcon |
| `iconLabel` | `string \| undefined` | The accessible label for the leading icon. This is passed to the icon's `label` prop and is read by screen readers to convey the icon's meaning. Defaults to a contextual string based on the `appearance`: - `neutral` → `'Calendar'` - `warning` → `'Warning'` - `danger` → `'Danger'` Set to `''` to mark the icon as decorative (when the label text alone is sufficient). |
| `isLoading` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true`, a spinner replaces the chevron icon and the trigger becomes non-interactive, indicating that an async operation is in progress (for example, saving a date selection). |
| `isSelected` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true`, renders the trigger in a selected/active state using the pressed background colour for the current appearance. Use this when the associated dropdown is open or the date has been chosen. |
| `isSpacious` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true`, increases the padding and height of the trigger to 32px and uses the body font size for more spacious layouts. |
| `label` | `string` | The text content to display inside the trigger (e.g. a formatted date string). (required) |
| `maxWidth` | `string \| number \| undefined` | The maximum width of the trigger. Accepts a number (treated as px) or a string (e.g. `'50%'`). Label text exceeding this width is truncated with an ellipsis. |
| `onClick` | `React.MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement> \| undefined` | Callback fired when the trigger button is clicked. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use to enable date selection—only open a dropdown or popup to allow changing the date.
- Use spacious sizing when displayed alongside buttons.
- Do not use to communicate other information about the date; use DateLabel instead for non-interactive date display.
- Do not use for date entry in forms; use DatePicker from @atlaskit/datetime-picker instead.

#### Content Guidelines
- Keep the date format concise and consistent with the surrounding experience.
- Do not rely on color alone; pair the appearance with clear date text.

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Do not rely on color alone to convey a date’s condition; ensure the date text is meaningful on its own.
- Ensure the trigger is operable by keyboard and exposes an accessible name.

## @atlaskit/datetime-picker Package
### DatePicker component
A component for selecting date values with calendar support.
- **Keywords:** date, picker, input, calendar, selection, form
- **Categories:** form
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import DatePicker from '@atlaskit/datetime-picker/date-picker';
import __noop from '@atlaskit/ds-lib/noop';
const Example = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<DatePicker
		clearControlLabel="Clear select date"
		onChange={__noop}
		shouldShowCalendarButton
		openCalendarLabel="open calendar"
	/>
);
export default Example;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `aria-describedby` | `string \| undefined` | Used to associate accessible descriptions to the date picker. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set the picker to autofocus on mount. |
| `calendarLabel` | `string \| undefined` | The aria-label attribute associated with the calendar. |
| `clearControlLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Set the `aria-label` for the clear button. Add the word "Clear" at the beginning of the clearControlLabel. For instance, for a field to set an appointment, use "Clear appointment date and time". |
| `dateFormat` | `string \| undefined` | Format the date with a string that is accepted by [date-fns's format function](https://date-fns.org/v1.29.0/docs/format). When set, the default parser also uses this format (via date-fns) so displayed labels re-parse. Without `dateFormat`, parsing falls back to the locale. A custom `parseInputValue` overrides this default. Note that though we are using `date-fns` version 2, we use [the tokens from `date-fns` version 1](https://date-fns.org/v1.30.1/docs/format) under the hood. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| undefined` | The default for `value`. |
| `disabled` | `string[] \| undefined` | An array of ISO dates that should be disabled on the calendar. This does not affect what users can type into the picker. |
| `disabledDateFilter` | `((date: string) => boolean) \| undefined` | A filter function for disabling dates on the calendar. This does not affect what users can type into the picker. The function is called with a date string in the format `YYYY-MM-DD` and should return `true` if the date should be disabled. |
| `formatDisplayLabel` | `((value: string, dateFormat: string) => string) \| undefined` | A function for formatting the date displayed in the input. By default composes together [`date-fns`'s parse method](https://date-fns.org/v1.29.0/docs/parse) and [`date-fns`'s format method](https://date-fns.org/v1.29.0/docs/format) to return a correctly formatted date string. Note that this does not affect how the input is parsed. Use `dateFormat` for default parsing of the display format, or `parseInputValue` for a custom parser. |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Set the id of the field. Associates a `<label></label>` with the field. |
| `inputLabel` | `string \| undefined` | The name of the input, used when `shouldShowCalendarButton` is true. See `shouldShowCalendarButton` description for more details. |
| `inputLabelId` | `string \| undefined` | The ID of the label for the input, used when `shouldShowCalendarButton` is true. See `shouldShowCalendarButton` description for more details. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the picker is disabled. |
| `isInvalid` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the picker has an invalid value. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the picker is open. |
| `isRequired` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set the field as required. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | Accessible name for the Date Picker Select, rendered as `aria-label`. This will override any other method of providing a label. |
| `locale` | `string \| undefined` | Locale used to format the date and calendar. See [DateTimeFormat](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/DateTimeFormat). |
| `maxDate` | `string \| undefined` | The latest enabled date. Dates after this are disabled on the calendar. This does not affect what users can type into the picker. |
| `minDate` | `string \| undefined` | The earliest enabled date. Dates before this are disabled on the calendar. This does not affect what users can type into the picker. |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | The name of the field. |
| `nextMonthLabel` | `string \| undefined` | The aria-label attribute associated with the next-month arrow. |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> \| undefined` | Called when the field is blurred. |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| undefined` | Called when the value changes. The only argument is an ISO time or empty string. |
| `onFocus` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> \| undefined` | Called when the field is focused. |
| `openCalendarLabel` | `string \| undefined` | The label associated with the button to open the calendar, rendered via the `shouldShowCalendarButton` prop. If a `label` prop is provided, this calendar button label will be prefixed by the value of `label`. If no `label` prop is provided, this prefix should be manually added. For example, ```tsx <label id="label" htmlFor="datepicker">Desired Appointment Date</label> <DatePicker id="datepicker" shouldShowCalendarButton inputLabel="Desired Appointment Date" openCalendarLabel="open calendar" /> ``` |
| `parseInputValue` | `((date: string, dateFormat: string) => Date) \| undefined` | A function for parsing input characters and transforming them into a Date object. Overrides the default parser. By default, when `dateFormat` is set the input is parsed with that format via date-fns; otherwise the date string is parsed based off the locale. Note that this does not affect how the resulting value is displayed in the input. Use the `dateFormat` or `formatDisplayLabel` prop to handle how the value is displayed. |
| `placeholder` | `string \| undefined` | Placeholder text displayed in input. |
| `previousMonthLabel` | `string \| undefined` | The aria-label attribute associated with the previous-month arrow. |
| `selectProps` | `(Omit<SelectProps<OptionType, false>, "aria-describedby" \| "aria-label" \| "placeholder" \| "inputId"> & { 'aria-describedby'?: undefined; 'aria-label'?: undefined; inputId?: undefined; placeholder?: undefined; } & { ...; }) \| undefined` |  |
| `shouldShowCalendarButton` | `boolean \| undefined` | Provides a functional calendar button that opens the calendar picker that lives on the right side of the date picker. The accessible name for this button is caculated using either the `label`, `inputLabel`, or `inputLabelId` props, along with the `openCalendarLabel` prop. |
| `spacing` | `Spacing \| undefined` | The spacing for the select control. Compact is `gridSize() * 4`, default is `gridSize * 5`. |
| `value` | `string \| undefined` | The ISO time used as the input value. |
| `weekStartDay` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| undefined` | Start day of the week for the calendar. - `0` sunday (default value) - `1` monday - `2` tuesday - `3` wednesday - `4` thursday - `5` friday - `6` saturday |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use for date selection only
- Provide clear date formats
- Handle date validation appropriately
- Consider calendar button visibility

#### Content Guidelines
- Use clear, descriptive labels
- Provide helpful placeholder text
- Keep labels concise but descriptive
- Use locale prop for date format localization

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Ensure proper keyboard navigation
- Use appropriate date formats
- Provide clear date labels
- Consider screen reader announcements

### DateTimePicker component
A component for selecting both date and time values.
- **Keywords:** datetime, picker, date, time, input, calendar
- **Categories:** form
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import DateTimePicker from '@atlaskit/datetime-picker/date-time-picker';
import __noop from '@atlaskit/ds-lib/noop';
const Example = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<DateTimePicker
		clearControlLabel="Clear date / time picker (editable times)"
		defaultValue="2018-01-02T14:30+10:00"
		onChange={__noop}
		timePickerProps={{
			timeIsEditable: true,
			label: 'Time picker (editable)',
			shouldShowTimeButton: true,
		}}
		datePickerProps={{
			label: 'Date picker (editable times)',
			shouldShowCalendarButton: true,
			openCalendarLabel: 'open calendar',
		}}
	/>
);
export default Example;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `aria-describedby` | `string \| undefined` | Used to associate accessible descriptions to both the date and time picker. If you want to associate individual accessible descriptions, this should be done through the `aria-describedby` props on the `datePickerProps` and `timePickerProps`. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set the picker to autofocus on mount. |
| `clearControlLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Set the `aria-label` for the clear button. Add the word "Clear" at the beginning of the clearControlLabel. For instance, for a field to set an appointment, use "Clear appointment date and time". |
| `datePickerProps` | `DatePickerBaseProps \| undefined` | Props applied to the `DatePicker`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| undefined` | The default for `value`. |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Set the id of the field. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the field is disabled. |
| `isInvalid` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the picker has an invalid value. |
| `isRequired` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set the field as required. |
| `locale` | `string \| undefined` | Locale used for formatting dates and times. See [DateTimeFormat](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/DateTimeFormat). |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | The name of the field. |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> \| undefined` | Called when the field is blurred. |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| undefined` | Called when the value changes and the date / time is a complete value, or empty. The only value is an ISO string or empty string. |
| `onFocus` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> \| undefined` | Called when the field is focused. |
| `parseValue` | `((dateTimeValue: string, date: string, time: string, timezone: string) => { dateValue: string; timeValue: string; zoneValue: string; }) \| undefined` | Function used to parse datetime values into their date, time and timezone sub-values. * |
| `spacing` | `Spacing \| undefined` | The spacing for the select control. Compact is `gridSize() * 4`, default is `gridSize() * 5`. |
| `timePickerProps` | `TimePickerBaseProps \| undefined` | Props applied to the `TimePicker`. |
| `value` | `string \| undefined` | The ISO time that should be used as the input value. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use for combined date and time selection
- Provide clear date/time formats
- Handle timezone considerations
- Consider validation requirements

#### Content Guidelines
- Use clear, descriptive labels
- Provide helpful placeholder text
- Use appropriate date/time formats
- Keep labels concise but descriptive
- Use locale prop for date and time format localization

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Ensure proper keyboard navigation
- Use appropriate date/time formats
- Provide clear date/time labels
- Consider screen reader announcements

### TimePicker component
A component for selecting time values with clock interface.
- **Keywords:** time, picker, input, clock, selection, form
- **Categories:** form
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import TimePicker from '@atlaskit/datetime-picker/time-picker';
import __noop from '@atlaskit/ds-lib/noop';
const Example = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<TimePicker
		clearControlLabel="Clear select time (editable)"
		defaultValue="14:30"
		onChange={__noop}
		timeFormat="HH:mm:ss A"
		timeIsEditable
		shouldShowTimeButton
		selectProps={{
			classNamePrefix: 'timepicker-select',
		}}
	/>
);
export default Example;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `aria-describedby` | `string \| undefined` | Used to associate accessible descriptions to the time picker. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set the picker to autofocus on mount. |
| `clearControlLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Set the `aria-label` for the clear button. Add the word "Clear" at the beginning of the clearControlLabel. For instance, for a field to set an appointment, use "Clear appointment date and time". |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| undefined` | The default for `value`. |
| `formatDisplayLabel` | `((time: string, timeFormat: string) => string) \| undefined` | A function for formatting the displayed time value in the input. By default parses with an internal time parser, and formats using the [date-fns format function]((https://date-fns.org/v1.29.0/docs/format)). Note that this does not affect how the input is parsed. This must be done using the `parseInputValue` prop. |
| `hideIcon` | `boolean \| undefined` | Hides icon for dropdown indicator. |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Set the id of the field. Associates a `<label></label>` with the field. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the field is disabled. |
| `isInvalid` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the picker has an invalid value. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if the dropdown is open. Will be `false` if not provided. |
| `isRequired` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set the field as required. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | Accessible name for the Time Picker Select, rendered as `aria-label`. This will override any other method of providing a label. |
| `locale` | `string \| undefined` | Locale used to format the time. See [DateTimeFormat](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/DateTimeFormat). |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | The name of the field. |
| `onBlur` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLElement> \| undefined` | Called when the field is blurred. |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| undefined` | Called when the value changes. The only argument is an ISO time or empty string. |
| `onFocus` | `FocusEventHandler<HTMLElement> \| undefined` | Called when the field is focused. |
| `openTimeLabel` | `string \| undefined` | The accessible label for the button that opens the time picker. When `label` is provided, it is prefixed to this label. |
| `parseInputValue` | `((time: string, timeFormat: string) => string \| Date) \| undefined` | A function for parsing input characters and transforming them into either a string or a Date object. By default parses the string based off the locale. Note that this does not affect how the resulting value is displayed in the input. To handle this, use either the `timeFormat` or `formatDisplayLabel` prop. |
| `placeholder` | `string \| undefined` | Placeholder text displayed in input. |
| `selectProps` | `DateTimePickerSelectProps \| undefined` |  |
| `shouldShowTimeButton` | `boolean \| undefined` | Provides a functional clock button that opens the time picker. When enabled, focusing the input with the keyboard does not open the menu; use this button, click the input, or type to open it instead. |
| `spacing` | `Spacing \| undefined` | The spacing for the select control. Compact is `gridSize() * 4`, default is `gridSize * 5`. |
| `timeFormat` | `string \| undefined` | Format the time with a string that is accepted by [date-fns's format function](https://date-fns.org/v1.29.0/docs/format). **This does not affect how the input is parsed.** This must be done using the `parseInputValue` prop. Note that though we are using `date-fns` version 2, we use [the tokens from `date-fns` version 1](https://date-fns.org/v1.30.1/docs/format) under the hood. |
| `timeIsEditable` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set if users can edit the input, allowing them to add custom times. |
| `times` | `string[] \| undefined` | The times shown in the dropdown. |
| `value` | `string \| undefined` | The ISO time that should be used as the input value. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use for time selection only
- Provide clear time formats
- Handle time validation appropriately
- Consider editable time input

#### Content Guidelines
- Use clear, descriptive labels
- Provide helpful placeholder text
- Use appropriate time formats
- Keep labels concise but descriptive
- Use locale prop for time format localization (e.g. 12h vs 24h)

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Ensure proper keyboard navigation
- Use appropriate time formats
- Provide clear time labels
- Consider screen reader announcements

## @atlaskit/dropdown-menu Package
### DropdownItem component
A dropdown item populates the dropdown menu with items. Use for links or actions; every item must be inside a DropdownItemGroup. Can also be used as the trigger for a nested submenu.
- **Keywords:** dropdown, menu, item, action, link, menuitem
- **Categories:** navigation
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import IconButton from '@atlaskit/button/icon/button';
import DropdownMenu from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu';
import DropdownItem from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item';
import DropdownItemGroup from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item-group';
import MoreIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/show-more-horizontal';
const Examples = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<>
		<DropdownMenu
			shouldRenderToParent
			trigger={({ triggerRef, ...props }) => (
				<IconButton ref={triggerRef} {...props} icon={MoreIcon} label="More" />
			)}
		>
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem href="/dashboard">Dashboard</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Create</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Delete</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
		<DropdownMenu shouldRenderToParent trigger="Actions">
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem>Export</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Share</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
	</>
);
export default Examples;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `aria-haspopup` | `boolean \| "grid" \| "dialog" \| "menu" \| "listbox" \| "tree" \| undefined` | An optional boolean value used to indicate if the dropdown item has popup or not. |
| `children` | `string \| number \| boolean \| ReactElement<any, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<ReactNode> \| ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Primary content for the item. (required) |
| `component` | `ComponentType<PropsWithChildren<CustomItemComponentProps>> \| undefined` | Custom component to render as an item. Should be wrapped in `forwardRef` to avoid accessibility issues when controlling keyboard focus. |
| `description` | `string \| global.JSX.Element \| undefined` | Description of the item. This will render smaller text below the primary text of the item as well as slightly increasing the height of the item. |
| `elemAfter` | `string \| number \| boolean \| ReactElement<any, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<ReactNode> \| ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Element to render after the item text. Generally should be an [icon](https://atlaskit.atlassian.com/packages/design-system/icon) component. |
| `elemBefore` | `string \| number \| boolean \| ReactElement<any, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<ReactNode> \| ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Element to render before the item text. Generally should be an [icon](https://atlaskit.atlassian.com/packages/design-system/icon) component. |
| `href` | `string \| undefined` | Link to another page. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Makes the element appear disabled. This will remove interactivity and the item won't appear in the focus order. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean \| undefined` | Makes the element appear selected. |
| `onClick` | `((e: MouseEvent<Element, globalThis.MouseEvent> \| KeyboardEvent<Element>) => void) \| undefined` | Event that is triggered when the element is clicked. |
| `rel` | `string \| undefined` | The relationship of the linked URL as space-separated link types. Generally you'll want to set this to "noopener noreferrer" when `target` is "_blank". |
| `returnFocusRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement> \| undefined` | If ref is passed, focus returns to that specific ref element after dropdown item clicked. |
| `role` | `string \| undefined` | An optional string value that specifies the role of the dropdown item. Use this to indicate whether the item is or presentational (e.g., 'presentation') for accessibility purposes. If not specified, it defaults to role="menuitem". |
| `shouldDescriptionWrap` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true` the description of the item will wrap multiple lines if it exceeds the width of the dropdown menu. |
| `shouldTitleWrap` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true` the title of the item will wrap multiple lines if it exceeds the width of the dropdown menu. |
| `target` | `string \| undefined` | Where to display the linked URL, see [anchor information](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a) on mdn for more information. |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | Adds a title attribute to the root item element. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use inside DropdownMenu with DropdownItemGroup (required parent)
- Use for links (href) or actions (onClick); verbs for actions, nouns for links; no articles; single line per item
- For a nested submenu: use as the trigger (pass triggerRef and trigger props, use elemAfter e.g. chevron); keep to maximum two layers

#### Content Guidelines
- Use clear, descriptive menu item labels
- Keep menu item text concise
- Use consistent terminology across menu items

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Avoid truncation—ensure max width does not cut off labels
- Ensure keyboard navigation with arrow keys

### DropdownItemGroup component
Wrapping element for dropdown menu items. Use to group related items; optional short uppercase title (e.g. "Edit page", "Tools") separates sections.
- **Keywords:** dropdown, menu, group, section, title
- **Categories:** navigation
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import IconButton from '@atlaskit/button/icon/button';
import DropdownMenu from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu';
import DropdownItem from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item';
import DropdownItemGroup from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item-group';
import MoreIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/show-more-horizontal';
const Examples = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<>
		<DropdownMenu
			shouldRenderToParent
			trigger={({ triggerRef, ...props }) => (
				<IconButton ref={triggerRef} {...props} icon={MoreIcon} label="More" />
			)}
		>
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem href="/dashboard">Dashboard</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Create</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Delete</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
		<DropdownMenu shouldRenderToParent trigger="Actions">
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem>Export</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Share</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
	</>
);
export default Examples;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `children` | `string \| number \| boolean \| ReactElement<any, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<ReactNode> \| ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Children of the section. This should generally be `Item` or `Heading` components, but can also be [`EmptyState`](https://atlaskit.atlassian.com/packages/design-system/empty-state)s if you want to render errors. (required) |
| `hasSeparator` | `boolean \| undefined` | Use this to render a border at the top of the section. |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | Unique identifier for the element. |
| `isList` | `boolean \| undefined` | If your menu contains a list, use this to add `<ul>` and `<li>` tags around the items. This is essential for offering better, accessible semantic markup in a list of items. |
| `isScrollable` | `boolean \| undefined` | Enables scrolling within the section. This won't work unless `maxHeight` is set on the parent `MenuGroup` component. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | Provide an accessible label for the section via `aria-label` for assistive technology. |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | The text passed into the internal `HeadingItem`. If a title isn't provided, the `HeadingItem` won't be rendered, and this component will act as a regular `Section`. |
| `titleId` | `string \| undefined` | ID referenced by the menu group wrapper's `aria-labelledby` attribute. This ID should be assigned to the group title element. Usage of either this, or the `label` attribute is strongly recommended. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use inside DropdownMenu to group related items
- Use short, uppercase title to describe the group
- Nested menu: maximum two layers

#### Content Guidelines
- Group related actions logically
- Use consistent terminology across menu items

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Provide clear group titles
- Nested menu: maximum two layers

### DropdownItemCheckbox component
A dropdown menu item with checkbox selection. Use for multiple selection from a list (e.g. status filters, show/hide toggles).
- **Keywords:** dropdown, menu, checkbox, multi-select, toggle
- **Categories:** navigation
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import IconButton from '@atlaskit/button/icon/button';
import DropdownMenu from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu';
import DropdownItem from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item';
import DropdownItemGroup from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item-group';
import MoreIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/show-more-horizontal';
const Examples = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<>
		<DropdownMenu
			shouldRenderToParent
			trigger={({ triggerRef, ...props }) => (
				<IconButton ref={triggerRef} {...props} icon={MoreIcon} label="More" />
			)}
		>
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem href="/dashboard">Dashboard</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Create</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Delete</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
		<DropdownMenu shouldRenderToParent trigger="Actions">
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem>Export</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Share</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
	</>
);
export default Examples;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `children` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Primary content for the item. (required) |
| `defaultSelected` | `boolean \| undefined` | Sets whether the checkbox begins selected. |
| `description` | `string \| JSX.Element \| undefined` | Description of the item. This will render smaller text below the primary text of the item as well as slightly increasing the height of the item. |
| `id` | `string` | Unique id of a checkbox. (required) |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Makes the checkbox appear disabled as well as removing interactivity. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean \| undefined` | Sets whether the checkbox is checked or unchecked. |
| `onClick` | `((e: React.MouseEvent<Element, globalThis.MouseEvent> \| React.KeyboardEvent<Element>) => void) \| undefined` | Event that is triggered when the checkbox is clicked. |
| `shouldDescriptionWrap` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true` the description of the item will wrap multiple lines if it's long enough. |
| `shouldTitleWrap` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true` the title of the item will wrap multiple lines if it's long enough. |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | Adds a title attribute to the root item element. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use with DropdownItemCheckboxGroup; control selection with isSelected and onClick
- Use for multiple selection from a list or toggles (e.g. categories, column visibility)
- Group related checkboxes; use short uppercase title on DropdownItemCheckboxGroup

#### Content Guidelines
- Use clear, descriptive labels
- Keep menu item text concise

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Ensure keyboard navigation and clear selection state
- Use appropriate ARIA attributes

### DropdownItemCheckboxGroup component
Groups DropdownItemCheckbox components for multi-select options within a dropdown menu.
- **Keywords:** dropdown, menu, checkbox, group, multi-select
- **Categories:** navigation
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import DropdownItemCheckbox from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-item-checkbox';
import DropdownItemCheckboxGroup from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-item-checkbox-group';
import DropdownMenu from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu';
const DropdownItemCheckboxExample = (): React.JSX.Element => {
	const [checked, setChecked] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({
		todo: true,
	});
	const toggle = (name: string) => {
		setChecked((prev) => ({
			...prev,
			[name]: !prev[name],
		}));
	};
	return (
		<DropdownMenu trigger="Status" shouldRenderToParent>
			<DropdownItemCheckboxGroup title="Categories" id="actions">
				<DropdownItemCheckbox id="todo" onClick={() => toggle('todo')} isSelected={checked['todo']}>
					To do
				</DropdownItemCheckbox>
				<DropdownItemCheckbox
					id="inprogress"
					onClick={() => toggle('inprogress')}
					isSelected={checked['inprogress']}
				>
					In progress
				</DropdownItemCheckbox>
				<DropdownItemCheckbox id="done" onClick={() => toggle('done')} isSelected={checked['done']}>
					Done
				</DropdownItemCheckbox>
			</DropdownItemCheckboxGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
	);
};
export default DropdownItemCheckboxExample;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `children` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Children of the section. This should generally be `Item` or `Heading` components, but can also be [`EmptyState`](https://atlaskit.atlassian.com/packages/design-system/empty-state)s if you want to render errors. (required) |
| `hasSeparator` | `boolean \| undefined` | Use this to render a border at the top of the section. |
| `id` | `string` | Unique identifier for the checkbox group. (required) |
| `isList` | `boolean \| undefined` | If your menu contains a list, use this to add `<ul>` and `<li>` tags around the items. This is essential for offering better, accessible semantic markup in a list of items. |
| `isScrollable` | `boolean \| undefined` | Enables scrolling within the section. This won't work unless `maxHeight` is set on the parent `MenuGroup` component. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | Provide an accessible label for the section via `aria-label` for assistive technology. |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | The text passed into the internal `HeadingItem`. If a title isn't provided, the `HeadingItem` won't be rendered, and this component will act as a regular `Section`. |
| `titleId` | `string \| undefined` | ID referenced by the menu group wrapper's `aria-labelledby` attribute. This ID should be assigned to the group title element. Usage of either this, or the `label` attribute is strongly recommended. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use to group related DropdownItemCheckbox items
- Use for multiple selection from a list

#### Content Guidelines
- Group related checkboxes logically
- Use consistent terminology

### DropdownItemRadio component
A dropdown menu item with radio selection. Use for single selection from a short list (e.g. view mode, sort order).
- **Keywords:** dropdown, menu, radio, single-select, choice
- **Categories:** navigation
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import IconButton from '@atlaskit/button/icon/button';
import DropdownMenu from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu';
import DropdownItem from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item';
import DropdownItemGroup from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item-group';
import MoreIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/show-more-horizontal';
const Examples = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<>
		<DropdownMenu
			shouldRenderToParent
			trigger={({ triggerRef, ...props }) => (
				<IconButton ref={triggerRef} {...props} icon={MoreIcon} label="More" />
			)}
		>
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem href="/dashboard">Dashboard</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Create</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Delete</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
		<DropdownMenu shouldRenderToParent trigger="Actions">
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem>Export</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Share</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
	</>
);
export default Examples;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `children` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Primary content for the item. (required) |
| `defaultSelected` | `boolean \| undefined` | Sets whether the checkbox begins selected. |
| `description` | `string \| JSX.Element \| undefined` | Description of the item. This will render smaller text below the primary text of the item as well as slightly increasing the height of the item. |
| `id` | `string` | Unique ID of the checkbox. (required) |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Makes the checkbox appear disabled as well as removing interactivity. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean \| undefined` | Sets whether the checkbox is checked or unchecked. |
| `onClick` | `((e: React.MouseEvent<Element, globalThis.MouseEvent> \| React.KeyboardEvent<Element>) => void) \| undefined` | Event that is triggered when the checkbox is clicked. |
| `shouldDescriptionWrap` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true` the description of the item will wrap multiple lines if it's long enough. |
| `shouldTitleWrap` | `boolean \| undefined` | When `true` the title of the item will wrap multiple lines if it's long enough. |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | Adds a title attribute to the root item element. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use with DropdownItemRadioGroup; control selection with isSelected and onClick
- Use for single selection from a short list (e.g. views, density)
- Group related radio items; use short uppercase title on DropdownItemRadioGroup

#### Content Guidelines
- Use clear, descriptive labels
- Keep menu item text concise

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Ensure keyboard navigation and clear selection state
- Use appropriate ARIA attributes

### DropdownItemRadioGroup component
Groups DropdownItemRadio components for single-select options within a dropdown menu.
- **Keywords:** dropdown, menu, radio, group, single-select
- **Categories:** navigation
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import DropdownItemRadio from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-item-radio';
import DropdownItemRadioGroup from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-item-radio-group';
import DropdownMenu from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu';
const DropdownItemRadioExample = (): React.JSX.Element => {
	const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string>('detail');
	return (
		<DropdownMenu trigger="Views" shouldRenderToParent>
			<DropdownItemRadioGroup title="Views" id="actions">
				<DropdownItemRadio
					id="detail"
					onClick={() => setSelected('detail')}
					isSelected={selected === 'detail'}
				>
					Detail view
				</DropdownItemRadio>
				<DropdownItemRadio
					id="list"
					onClick={() => setSelected('list')}
					isSelected={selected === 'list'}
				>
					List view
				</DropdownItemRadio>
			</DropdownItemRadioGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
	);
};
export default DropdownItemRadioExample;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `children` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Children of the section. This should generally be `Item` or `Heading` components, but can also be [`EmptyState`](https://atlaskit.atlassian.com/packages/design-system/empty-state)s if you want to render errors. (required) |
| `hasSeparator` | `boolean \| undefined` | Use this to render a border at the top of the section. |
| `id` | `string` |  (required) |
| `isList` | `boolean \| undefined` | If your menu contains a list, use this to add `<ul>` and `<li>` tags around the items. This is essential for offering better, accessible semantic markup in a list of items. |
| `isScrollable` | `boolean \| undefined` | Enables scrolling within the section. This won't work unless `maxHeight` is set on the parent `MenuGroup` component. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | Provide an accessible label for the section via `aria-label` for assistive technology. |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | The text passed into the internal `HeadingItem`. If a title isn't provided, the `HeadingItem` won't be rendered, and this component will act as a regular `Section`. |
| `titleId` | `string \| undefined` | ID referenced by the menu group wrapper's `aria-labelledby` attribute. This ID should be assigned to the group title element. Usage of either this, or the `label` attribute is strongly recommended. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use to group related DropdownItemRadio items
- Use for single selection from a short list

#### Content Guidelines
- Group related radio items logically
- Use consistent terminology

### DropdownMenu component
A dropdown menu component for displaying contextual actions and options.
- **Keywords:** dropdown, menu, overflow, actions, options, popup, contextual
- **Categories:** navigation
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import IconButton from '@atlaskit/button/icon/button';
import DropdownMenu from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu';
import DropdownItem from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item';
import DropdownItemGroup from '@atlaskit/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu-item-group';
import MoreIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/show-more-horizontal';
const Examples = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<>
		<DropdownMenu
			shouldRenderToParent
			trigger={({ triggerRef, ...props }) => (
				<IconButton ref={triggerRef} {...props} icon={MoreIcon} label="More" />
			)}
		>
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem href="/dashboard">Dashboard</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Create</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Delete</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
		<DropdownMenu shouldRenderToParent trigger="Actions">
			<DropdownItemGroup>
				<DropdownItem>Export</DropdownItem>
				<DropdownItem>Share</DropdownItem>
			</DropdownItemGroup>
		</DropdownMenu>
	</>
);
export default Examples;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `appearance` | `"default" \| "tall" \| undefined` | Controls the appearance of the menu. The default menu will scroll after its height exceeds the pre-defined amount. The tall menu won't scroll until the height exceeds the height of the viewport. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean \| undefined` | Controls if the first menu item receives focus when menu is opened. Note that the menu has a focus lock which traps the focus within the menu. The first item gets focus automatically if the menu is triggered using the keyboard. |
| `children` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Content that will be rendered inside the layer element. Should typically be `DropdownItemGroup` or `DropdownItem`, or the checkbox and radio variants of those. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean \| undefined` | Controls the initial open state of the dropdown. If provided, the component is considered to be controlled which means that the user is responsible for managing the open and close state of the menu. Using `defaultOpen` may cause accessiblity issues because it will automatically shift focus to the first menu item; which can be disorienting. Only use this if action on the menu is required to proceed. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean \| undefined` | If true, a spinner is rendered instead of the items. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean \| undefined` | Controls the open state of the dropdown. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | Provide an accessible label via `aria-label` for assistive technology. |
| `menuLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Provide an accessible label for the menu element for assistive technology. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((args: OnOpenChangeArgs) => void) \| undefined` | Called when the menu should be open/closed. Receives an object with `isOpen` state. If the dropdown was closed programatically, the `event` parameter will be `null`. |
| `placement` | `Placement \| undefined` | Position of the menu. |
| `returnFocusRef` | `React.RefObject<HTMLElement> \| undefined` | If ref is passed, focus returns to that specific ref element after dropdown dismissed. |
| `shouldFitContainer` | `boolean \| undefined` | This fits the dropdown menu width to its parent's width. When set to `true`, the trigger and dropdown menu elements will be wrapped in a `div` with `position: relative`. The dropdown menu will be rendered as a sibling to the trigger element, and will be full width. The default is `false`. This fits the dropdown menu width to its parent's width. When set to `true`, the trigger and dropdown menu elements will be wrapped in a `div` with `position: relative`. The dropdown menu will be rendered as a sibling to the trigger element, and will be full width. The default is `false`. |
| `shouldIgnoreCloseEvent` | `((event: Event \| React.MouseEvent<Element, MouseEvent> \| React.KeyboardEvent<Element>) => boolean) \| undefined` | Allows consumers to ignore specific close events, for example when an external overlay should be treated as part of the dropdown interaction. |
| `spacing` | `SpacingMode \| undefined` | Controls the spacing density of the menu. |
| `statusLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Text to be used as status for assistive technologies. Defaults to "Loading". |
| `trigger` | `string \| ((triggerButtonProps: CustomTriggerProps<T>) => React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>>) \| undefined` | Content that triggers the dropdown menu to open and close. Use with `triggerType` to get a button trigger. To customize the trigger element, provide a function to this prop. You can find [examples for custom triggers](https://atlassian.design/components/dropdown-menu/examples#custom-triggers) in our documentation. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use for 5–15 items; navigation or command (action on selection)
- Avoid truncation—check max width; avoid truncated labels
- Nested menu: maximum two layers
- In a modal, use shouldRenderToParent for correct focus and screen reader behavior
- Disabled triggers are not supported (see Button a11y)
- Use Select for search/select; Checkbox for multiple from list; Radio for short single choice

#### Content Guidelines
- Logical order (e.g. most selected first); group with uppercase section title
- Use verbs for actions, nouns for links; no articles; single line per item
- Use clear, descriptive menu item labels
- Keep menu item text concise
- Group related actions logically
- Use consistent terminology across menu items

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Avoid truncation—ensure max width does not cut off labels
- Focus lock when open; keyboard open should focus first item
- Nested menu: maximum two layers
- In modal use shouldRenderToParent for focus and voicing
- Provide clear labels for dropdown triggers
- Ensure keyboard navigation with arrow keys
- Use appropriate ARIA attributes

## @atlaskit/dynamic-table Package
### Dynamic table component
A dynamic table displays rows of data with built-in pagination, sorting, and re-ordering functionality.
- **Keywords:** table, dynamic-table, data, sortable, rows, columns, sorting, pagination, drag and drop, ranking
- **Categories:** data display
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import DynamicTable from '@atlaskit/dynamic-table/stateful';
import { head, rows } from './content/sample-data';
export default function TableUncontrolled(): React.JSX.Element {
	return (
		<DynamicTable
			head={head}
			rows={rows}
			rowsPerPage={5}
			defaultPage={1}
			loadingSpinnerSize="large"
			isRankable
			testId="table"
		/>
	);
}
```
#### Example
```tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import Banner from '@atlaskit/banner/banner';
import ButtonGroup from '@atlaskit/button/button-group';
import Button from '@atlaskit/button/default/button';
import { cssMap } from '@atlaskit/css';
import DynamicTableStateless from '@atlaskit/dynamic-table/stateless';
import WarningIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/status-warning';
import { Flex } from '@atlaskit/primitives/compiled/flex';
import { token } from '@atlaskit/tokens';
import { head, rows } from './content/sample-data';
const iconSpacingStyles = cssMap({
	space050: {
		paddingBlock: token('space.050'),
		paddingInline: token('space.050'),
	},
});
export default function TableControlled(): React.JSX.Element {
	const [pageNumber, setPageNumber] = useState(3);
	const navigateTo = (pageNumber: number) => {
		setPageNumber(pageNumber);
	};
	return (
		<>
			<Banner
				appearance="warning"
				icon={
					<Flex xcss={iconSpacingStyles.space050}>
						<WarningIcon label="" />
					</Flex>
				}
			>
				This is a stateless table example, which doesn't have pagination support. To navigate pages,
				use the "Previous page" and "Next page" buttons.
			</Banner>
			<ButtonGroup label="Paging navigation">
				<Button isDisabled={pageNumber === 1} onClick={() => navigateTo(pageNumber - 1)}>
					Previous Page
				</Button>
				<Button isDisabled={pageNumber === 5} onClick={() => navigateTo(pageNumber + 1)}>
					Next Page
				</Button>
			</ButtonGroup>
			<DynamicTableStateless
				head={head}
				rows={rows}
				rowsPerPage={5}
				page={pageNumber}
				loadingSpinnerSize="large"
				isLoading={false}
				isFixedSize
				sortKey="term"
				sortOrder="DESC"
				onSort={() => console.log('onSort')}
				onSetPage={() => console.log('onSetPage')}
			/>
		</>
	);
}
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `caption` | `string \| number \| boolean \| ReactElement<any, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<ReactNode> \| ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Caption for the table styled as a heading. This appears before the table header, and is announced when people who use assistive technology land on the table. If you don’t want the caption to appear on the page but do want it to be available for assistive technology, surround the caption with `<VisuallyHidden>`. |
| `defaultPage` | `number \| undefined` | When the table is initially rendered, use this to set which page number is shown by default. In most circumstances, people will expect this to be page `1`. |
| `defaultSortKey` | `string \| undefined` | Sets which column the rows should be sorted by when the table is initially rendered. Corresponds to the `key`'s defined in the `head` prop. |
| `defaultSortOrder` | `SortOrderType \| undefined` | Default column sort order used when initially rendering. Defaults to `"ASC"`. |
| `emptyView` | `ReactElement<any, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| undefined` | Shown when the table has no content. |
| `head` | `HeadType \| undefined` | Cells to be placed in the head of the table. Never put controls, like links and buttons in the table header. Each element in the head creates a new column. |
| `highlightedRowIndex` | `number \| number[] \| undefined` | Use this to set if the row will be highlighted. Never use highlighted rows to indicate that a person has selected or focused on the row. |
| `isFixedSize` | `boolean \| undefined` | Use this to force columns to use their initial width regardless of the size of the content that loads in. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean \| undefined` | Displays a loading spinner overlaid on top of the current page. |
| `isRankable` | `boolean \| undefined` | Use this to enable drag and drop sorting of table rows. |
| `isRankingDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Disables being able to drop rows on the table. We recommend using `isRankable` instead of this prop, and it will be deprecated in a future release. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | If you don’t use a caption, then you’ll need to use label to describe the table for assistive technologies. Avoid using both at the same time as they may conflict. Rather than a screen reader speaking "Entering table", passing in an label allows a custom message like "Entering Jira work items table". |
| `loadingLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Use this to set a label for assistive technology that describes the loading state. The default label is "Loading table". You can customize this to be more specific to your table, for example “Loading work items table”. |
| `loadingSpinnerSize` | `LoadingSpinnerSizeType \| undefined` | Configuration of the loading spinner shown when `isLoading` is true. Defaults to `"large"` when a page has more than two rows, else `"small"`. |
| `onPageRowsUpdate` | `((pageRows: RowType[]) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when the rows displayed on a page have changed. |
| `onRankEnd` | `((rankEnd: RankEnd) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when a drop of a row has completed. |
| `onRankStart` | `((rankStart: RankStart) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when a drag of a row has started. |
| `onSetPage` | `((page: number, UIAnalyticsEvent?: UIAnalyticsEvent \| undefined) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when the table page has changed. |
| `onSort` | `((data: any, UIAnalyticsEvent?: UIAnalyticsEvent \| undefined) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when a column heading has been sorted. Use this to provide custom sorting. |
| `page` | `number \| undefined` | Page the table should show. |
| `paginationi18n` | `I18nShape \| undefined` | Labels for the previous and next buttons used in pagination. Defaults to `"Previous"` and `"Next"`. |
| `rows` | `RowType[] \| undefined` | Rows to be placed in the table. Each row contains cells which should map to the ones defined in the head. Rows accept standard HTML <tr> props in addition to those listed below. Ensure each cell has a unique `key` per column - this is used for both React's reconciliation of lists and column sorting. |
| `rowsPerPage` | `number \| undefined` | Use this to control how many rows should be displayed per page. If the number of rows exceed one page, this will enable pagination. |
| `sortKey` | `string \| undefined` | Column key that the rows should be sorted by. Corresponds to the `key`'s defined in the `head` prop. |
| `sortOrder` | `SortOrderType \| undefined` | Column sort order. |

### DynamicTableStateless component
A stateless dynamic table for when you need to control pagination, sorting, and data externally. Use when integrating with custom state management.
- **Keywords:** table, dynamic-table, stateless, controlled, pagination, sorting
- **Categories:** data display
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import Banner from '@atlaskit/banner/banner';
import ButtonGroup from '@atlaskit/button/button-group';
import Button from '@atlaskit/button/default/button';
import { cssMap } from '@atlaskit/css';
import DynamicTableStateless from '@atlaskit/dynamic-table/stateless';
import WarningIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/status-warning';
import { Flex } from '@atlaskit/primitives/compiled/flex';
import { token } from '@atlaskit/tokens';
import { head, rows } from './content/sample-data';
const iconSpacingStyles = cssMap({
	space050: {
		paddingBlock: token('space.050'),
		paddingInline: token('space.050'),
	},
});
export default function TableControlled(): React.JSX.Element {
	const [pageNumber, setPageNumber] = useState(3);
	const navigateTo = (pageNumber: number) => {
		setPageNumber(pageNumber);
	};
	return (
		<>
			<Banner
				appearance="warning"
				icon={
					<Flex xcss={iconSpacingStyles.space050}>
						<WarningIcon label="" />
					</Flex>
				}
			>
				This is a stateless table example, which doesn't have pagination support. To navigate pages,
				use the "Previous page" and "Next page" buttons.
			</Banner>
			<ButtonGroup label="Paging navigation">
				<Button isDisabled={pageNumber === 1} onClick={() => navigateTo(pageNumber - 1)}>
					Previous Page
				</Button>
				<Button isDisabled={pageNumber === 5} onClick={() => navigateTo(pageNumber + 1)}>
					Next Page
				</Button>
			</ButtonGroup>
			<DynamicTableStateless
				head={head}
				rows={rows}
				rowsPerPage={5}
				page={pageNumber}
				loadingSpinnerSize="large"
				isLoading={false}
				isFixedSize
				sortKey="term"
				sortOrder="DESC"
				onSort={() => console.log('onSort')}
				onSetPage={() => console.log('onSetPage')}
			/>
		</>
	);
}
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `caption` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Caption for the table styled as a heading. This appears before the table header, and is announced when people who use assistive technology land on the table. If you don’t want the caption to appear on the page but do want it to be available for assistive technology, surround the caption with `<VisuallyHidden>`. |
| `emptyView` | `React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| undefined` | Shown when the table has no content. |
| `head` | `HeadType \| undefined` | Cells to be placed in the head of the table. Each element in the head creates a new column. |
| `highlightedRowIndex` | `number \| number[] \| undefined` | Use this to set which rows will be highlighted. Never use highlighted rows to indicate that a person has selected or focused on the row. |
| `isFixedSize` | `boolean \| undefined` | Use this to force columns to use their initial width regardless of the size of the content that loads in. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean \| undefined` | Displays a loading spinner overlaid on top of the current page. |
| `isRankable` | `boolean \| undefined` | Use this to enable drag and drop sorting of table rows. |
| `isRankingDisabled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Disables being able to drop rows on the table. We recommend using `isRankable` instead of this prop, and it will be deprecated in a future release. |
| `label` | `string \| undefined` | If you don’t use a caption, then you’ll need to use label to describe the table for assistive technologies. Avoid using both at the same time as they may conflict. Rather than a screen reader speaking "Entering table", passing in an label allows a custom message like "Entering Jira work items table". |
| `loadingLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Accessible name for loading states spinner. Can be used for internationalization. Default is "Loading table". |
| `loadingSpinnerSize` | `LoadingSpinnerSizeType \| undefined` | Sets the size of the loading spinner when `isLoading` is true. Defaults to `"large"` when a page has more than two rows, otherwise it will be `"small"`. |
| `onPageRowsUpdate` | `((pageRows: RowType[]) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when the rows displayed on a page have changed. |
| `onRankEnd` | `((rankEnd: RankEnd, uiAnalyticsEvent?: UIAnalyticsEvent \| undefined) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when a drop of a row has completed. |
| `onRankStart` | `((rankStart: RankStart) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when a drag of a row has started. |
| `onSetPage` | `((page: number, UIAnalyticsEvent?: UIAnalyticsEvent \| undefined) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when the table page has changed. Use this when you want to control the pagination of the table. |
| `onSort` | `((data: any, UIAnalyticsEvent?: UIAnalyticsEvent \| undefined) => void) \| undefined` | A callback that happens when a column heading has been sorted. Use this to provide custom sorting for the table. |
| `page` | `number \| undefined` | Page the table should show. Set by default to 1, so that it's never undefined. |
| `paginationi18n` | `I18nShape \| undefined` | Labels for the pagination wrapper, previous and next buttons used in pagination. Defaults to `"Page"`, `"Pagination"`, `"Previous"` and `"Next"`. |
| `rows` | `RowType[] \| undefined` | Rows to be placed in the table. Each row contains cells which should map to the ones defined in the head. Ensure each cell has a unique `key` per column - this is used for both Reacts reconcilation of lists and column sorting. |
| `rowsPerPage` | `number \| undefined` | Controls how many rows should be displayed per page. |
| `sortKey` | `string \| undefined` | Column key that the rows should be sorted by. Corresponds to the `key`'s defined in the `head` prop. |
| `sortOrder` | `SortOrderType \| undefined` | Column sort order. |
| `totalRows` | `number \| undefined` | Total number of rows, in case of paginated data. |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use when you need to control table state externally (e.g. server-side pagination, custom sort logic)
- Use DynamicTable (stateful) when built-in pagination and sorting are sufficient

## @atlaskit/empty-state Package
### EmptyState component
A component for when there is nothing to display (no tasks, cleared inbox, no results).
- **Keywords:** empty, state, results, placeholder, no-content, void
- **Categories:** status
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import EmptyState from '@atlaskit/empty-state/empty-state';
const Examples = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<>
		<EmptyState header="No items" description="Add items to get started" />
		<EmptyState
			header="No search results"
			description="Try adjusting your search criteria or browse all items."
		/>
		<EmptyState
			header="Welcome to your dashboard"
			description="Create your first project to get started with the platform."
		/>
	</>
);
export default Examples;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `buttonGroupLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Accessible name for the action buttons group of empty state. Can be used for internationalization. Default is "Button group". |
| `description` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | The main block of text that holds additional supporting information. |
| `header` | `string` | Title that briefly describes the page to the user. (required) |
| `headingLevel` | `number \| undefined` | The value used to set the heading level of the header element. Must be in the range of 1 to 6. Defaults to 4. |
| `headingSize` | `"xsmall" \| "medium" \| undefined` | The keyword used to set the visual appearance of the header element. Defaults to "medium". "xsmall" can be used for empty states in smaller contexts such as popups. |
| `imageHeight` | `number \| undefined` | Height of the image that is rendered in EmptyState component. Useful when you want image to be of exact height to stop it bouncing around when loading in. Only set `height` if you want the image to resize down on smaller devices. |
| `imageUrl` | `string \| undefined` | The url of image that will be shown above the title, fed directly into the `src` prop of an <img> element. Note, this image will be constrained by the `maxWidth` and `maxHeight` props. |
| `imageWidth` | `number \| undefined` | Width of the image that is rendered in EmptyState component. Useful when you want image to be of exact width to stop it bouncing around when loading in. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean \| undefined` | Used to indicate a loading state. Will show a spinner next to the action buttons when true. |
| `maxImageHeight` | `number \| undefined` | Maximum height (in pixels) of the image, default value is 160. |
| `maxImageWidth` | `number \| undefined` | Maximum width (in pixels) of the image, default value is 160. |
| `primaryAction` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Primary action button for the page, usually it will be something like "Create" (or "Retry" for error pages). |
| `renderImage` | `((props: RenderImageProps) => React.ReactNode) \| undefined` | An alternative API to supply an image using a render prop. Only rendered if no `imageUrl` is supplied. |
| `secondaryAction` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Secondary action button for the page. |
| `tertiaryAction` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | Button with link to some external resource like documentation or tutorial, it will be opened in a new tab. |
| `width` | `Width \| undefined` | Controls how much horizontal space the component fills. Defaults to "wide". |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use when nothing to display in a view (no tasks, no results, cleared inbox)
- Header is required; illustration, description, and buttons are optional
- Use wide (464px) or narrow (304px) layout as appropriate
- Provide one primary CTA; do not stack multiple primary buttons
- Use illustration as spot only—do not resize; keep relevant, neutral or humorous
- Explain why the state is empty and provide clear next steps
- Consider i18n for illustrations (e.g. culturally neutral imagery, translatable alt text)

#### Content Guidelines
- Blank slate: inspirational, motivating tone
- All done: celebratory tone
- No results: neutral tone with next steps
- Use clear, descriptive headers
- Provide specific next steps; avoid negative language

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Avoid jargon; use simple language
- Use descriptive link text (not "click here")
- Add alt text only if the illustration is meaningful; otherwise omit or mark decorative
- Provide clear empty state messaging
- Use appropriate headings and structure
- Ensure actionable content is accessible

## @atlaskit/flag Package
### Flag component
A component for displaying brief messages.
- **Keywords:** flag, message, success, notification, alert, toast
- **Categories:** feedback
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import Flag from '@atlaskit/flag/flag';
import { FlagGroup } from '@atlaskit/flag/flag-group';
import InfoIcon from '@atlaskit/icon/core/status-information';
const Examples = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<>
		<FlagGroup>
			<Flag
				id="flag-1"
				icon={<InfoIcon label="Info" />}
				title="Success"
				description="Your changes have been saved successfully."
				appearance="success"
			/>
		</FlagGroup>
		<FlagGroup>
			<Flag
				id="flag-2"
				icon={<InfoIcon label="Warning" />}
				title="Warning"
				description="This action cannot be undone."
				appearance="warning"
				actions={[
					{
						content: 'Proceed',
						onClick: () => console.log('Proceed clicked'),
					},
				]}
			/>
		</FlagGroup>
		<FlagGroup>
			<Flag
				id="flag-3"
				icon={<InfoIcon label="Error" />}
				title="Error"
				description="Something went wrong. Please try again."
				appearance="error"
				actions={[
					{
						content: 'Retry',
						onClick: () => console.log('Retry clicked'),
					},
				]}
			/>
		</FlagGroup>
	</>
);
export default Examples;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `actions` | `ActionsType \| undefined` | Array of clickable actions to be shown at the bottom of the flag. For flags where appearance is 'normal', actions will be shown as links. For all other appearance values, actions will shown as buttons. If href is passed the action will be shown as a link with the passed href prop. |
| `appearance` | `AppearanceTypes \| undefined` | Makes the flag appearance bold. Setting this to anything other than 'normal' hides the dismiss button. |
| `autoDismissSeconds` | `number \| undefined` | Duration in seconds before flag gets auto dismissed. Default is 8 seconds. For a11y reasons 8s is also a strongly-suggested minimum. Only applies to auto-dismissable flags. |
| `delayAnnouncement` | `number \| undefined` | Milliseconds to delay the screen reader announcement due to announcement conflict. |
| `description` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | The secondary content shown below the flag title. |
| `headingLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| undefined` | Specifies the heading level in the document structure. If not specified, the default is `2`. |
| `icon` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | The icon displayed in the top-left of the flag. Should be an instance of `@atlaskit/icon`. Your icon will receive the appropriate default color, which you can override by setting the `color` prop on the icon to your preferred icon color. If no icon is provided, a default icon will be used based on the appearance prop. |
| `id` | `string \| number` | A unique identifier used for rendering and onDismissed callbacks. (required) |
| `linkComponent` | `React.ComponentType<CustomThemeButtonProps> \| undefined` | A link component that is passed down to the `@atlaskit/button` used by actions, to allow custom routers to be used. See the [button with router](https://atlaskit.atlassian.com/packages/design-system/button/example/ButtonWithRouter) example of what this component should look like. |
| `onBlur` | `((e: React.FocusEvent<HTMLElement, Element>, analyticsEvent: UIAnalyticsEvent) => void) \| undefined` | Standard onBlur event, applied to Flag by AutoDismissFlag. |
| `onDismissed` | `((id: string \| number, analyticsEvent: UIAnalyticsEvent) => void) \| undefined` | Handler which will be called when a Flag's dismiss button is clicked. Receives the id of the dismissed Flag as a parameter. |
| `onFocus` | `((e: React.FocusEvent<HTMLElement, Element>, analyticsEvent: UIAnalyticsEvent) => void) \| undefined` | Standard onFocus event, applied to Flag by AutoDismissFlag. |
| `onMouseOut` | `React.MouseEventHandler<Element> \| undefined` | Standard onMouseOut event, applied to Flag by AutoDismissFlag. |
| `onMouseOver` | `React.MouseEventHandler<Element> \| undefined` | Standard onMouseOver event, applied to Flag by AutoDismissFlag. |
| `title` | `string \| number \| boolean \| React.ReactElement<any, string \| React.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| Iterable<React.ReactNode> \| React.ReactPortal \| null \| undefined` | The bold text shown at the top of the flag. (required) |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use for confirmations and alerts needing minimal interaction
- Position at bottom left; overlays content
- Default: dismissible, event-driven (e.g. avatar update). Bold: not dismissible, severity (success/loading/warning/error), collapsed/expanded
- Use Banner for critical/system messages; Inline message when action is required; Modal for immediate action

#### Content Guidelines
- Be clear about what went wrong for errors
- Provide specific steps to resolve issues
- Use a helpful, non-threatening tone
- Clearly state potential consequences for warnings
- Confirm outcome then get out of the way for success messages
- Information: inform, no action needed
- Warning: before action, empathy, offer alternative
- Error: explain what went wrong and next step; use "we" not "you"
- Success: confirm outcome, then get out of the way; option to view details
- Be clear and concise; use a helpful, non-threatening tone

#### Accessibility Guidelines
- Keep copy concise for zoom and long words
- Use h2 for title via `headingLevel` prop; maintain heading hierarchy
- Do not stack dismissible and non-dismissible flags
- Do not rely on color alone for severity
- Avoid dead ends—always indicate how to proceed
- Do not use auto-dismiss for critical messages
- Use descriptive link text that describes the destination
- Ensure flag content is announced by screen readers
- Consider screen reader announcement conflicts

## @atlaskit/form Package
### CharacterCounter component
Displays character count for text inputs. Can be used standalone or with CharacterCounterField.
- **Keywords:** form, character, counter
- **Categories:** form
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { CharacterCounter } from '@atlaskit/form/character-counter';
import { Label } from '@atlaskit/form/label/default';
import { Box } from '@atlaskit/primitives/compiled/box';
import { Stack } from '@atlaskit/primitives/compiled/stack';
import TextArea from '@atlaskit/textarea/text-area';
import TextField from '@atlaskit/textfield/text-field';
/**
 * Standalone CharacterCounter example - used outside of Form context
 * This is useful when you need character counting in custom implementations
 * that don't use the Form component or have a specific layout requirements
 * that CharacterCounterField does not provide. Generally speaking, it is
 * recommended to use CharacterCounterField for consistent styling.
 */
const StandaloneCharacterCounterExample = (): React.JSX.Element => {
	const [textFieldValue, setTextFieldValue] = useState('');
	const [textAreaValue, setTextAreaValue] = useState('');
	const textFieldId = 'standalone-text-field';
	const textAreaId = 'standalone-text-area';
	// Character limits
	const maxCharacters = 50;
	const minCharacters = 10;
	const textAreaMaxCharacters = 200;
	// Calculate error states for styling
	const isTextFieldTooLong = textFieldValue.length > maxCharacters;
	const isTextAreaTooShort = textAreaValue.length < minCharacters;
	const isTextAreaTooLong = textAreaValue.length > textAreaMaxCharacters;
	const hasTextAreaError = isTextAreaTooShort || isTextAreaTooLong;
	return (
		<Stack space="space.200">
			{/* Example 1: TextField with maximum character limit */}
			<Box>
				<Label htmlFor={textFieldId}>Display name</Label>
				<TextField
					id={textFieldId}
					value={textFieldValue}
					onChange={(e) => setTextFieldValue(e.currentTarget.value)}
					aria-describedby={`${textFieldId}-character-counter`}
					isInvalid={isTextFieldTooLong}
				/>
				<CharacterCounter
					currentValue={textFieldValue}
					maxCharacters={maxCharacters}
					inputId={textFieldId}
					shouldShowAsError={isTextFieldTooLong}
				/>
			</Box>
			{/* Example 2: TextArea with both minimum and maximum limits */}
			<Box>
				<Label htmlFor={textAreaId}>Bio</Label>
				<TextArea
					id={textAreaId}
					value={textAreaValue}
					onChange={(e) => setTextAreaValue(e.currentTarget.value)}
					aria-describedby={`${textAreaId}-character-counter`}
					resize="auto"
					minimumRows={3}
					isInvalid={hasTextAreaError}
					isRequired
				/>
				<CharacterCounter
					currentValue={textAreaValue}
					minCharacters={minCharacters}
					maxCharacters={textAreaMaxCharacters}
					inputId={textAreaId}
					shouldShowAsError={hasTextAreaError}
				/>
			</Box>
		</Stack>
	);
};
export default StandaloneCharacterCounterExample;
```

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| `currentValue` | `string \| undefined` | Current value of the input field |
| `inputId` | `string \| undefined` | ID of the associated input for accessibility. Not needed if the character counter is used within CharacterCounterField. When provided, the character counter will have an ID of `${inputId}-character-counter` which should be referenced in the input's `aria-describedby` attribute. If not provided, will attempt to use InputId context from Form. |
| `maxCharacters` | `number \| undefined` | Maximum number of characters allowed (optional) |
| `minCharacters` | `number \| undefined` | Minimum number of characters required (optional) |
| `overMaximumMessage` | `string \| undefined` | Optional custom message to display when character limit is exceeded |
| `shouldShowAsError` | `boolean \| undefined` | Whether to style violations as errors (red text + icon). By default, violations are automatically styled as errors. In forms, set this to false to suppress error styling when the form hasn't flagged an error yet (e.g., field not touched). // Standalone: smart default (violations = errors) <CharacterCounter currentValue={value} maxCharacters={100} /> // Form: align with final-form error state <CharacterCounter currentValue={value} maxCharacters={100} shouldShowAsError={isCharacterCountViolation} /> |
| `underMaximumMessage` | `string \| undefined` | Optional custom message to display when character limit is not exceeded |
| `underMinimumMessage` | `string \| undefined` | Optional custom message to display when minimum character requirement is not met |

#### Usage Guidelines
- Use when displaying character count for text inputs
- Provide current length and max length
- Use CharacterCounterField for integrated form field experience

### CharacterCounterField component
A form field that includes character count display. Combines Field with CharacterCounter.
- **Keywords:** form, character, counter, field
- **Categories:** form
- **Status:** general-availability

#### Example
```tsx
import ButtonGroup from '@atlaskit/button/button-group';
import Button from '@atlaskit/button/default/button';
import { CharacterCounterField } from '@atlaskit/form/character-counter-field';
import { type FieldProps } from '@atlaskit/form/field';
import Form from '@atlaskit/form/form';
import { FormFooter } from '@atlaskit/form/form-footer';
import { FormHeader } from '@atlaskit/form/form-header';
import { FormSection } from '@atlaskit/form/form-section';
import { RequiredAsterisk } from '@atlaskit/form/required-asterisk';
import { Flex } from '@atlaskit/primitives/compiled/flex';
import { Text } from '@atlaskit/primitives/compiled/text';
import TextArea from '@atlaskit/textarea/text-area';
import TextField from '@atlaskit/textfield/text-field';
/**
 * Mock i18n setup - in a real app, these would come from your i18n library
 * Example: import { useIntl } from 'react-intl';
 */
const messages = {
	'bio.underMinimum': 'Enter at least {minimum} characters.',
	'bio.overMaximum': 'Your bio exceeds the maximum length of {maximum} characters',
};
// Mock formatMessage - in a real app: const { formatMessage } = useIntl();
const formatMessage = (
	messageDescriptor: { id: keyof typeof messages },
	values?: Record<string, string | number>,
): string => {
	let message = messages[messageDescriptor.id];
	if (values) {
		Object.entries(values).forEach(([key, value]) => {
			message = message.replace(new RegExp(`\\{${key}\\}`, 'g'), String(value));
		});
	}
	return message;
};
const FormCharacterCounterExample = (): React.JSX.Element => (
	<Flex direction="column">
		<Form
			noValidate
			onSubmit={(data) => {
				console.log('form data', data);
			}}
		>
			<FormHeader title="Profile">
				<Text as="p" aria-hidden="true">
					Required fields are marked with an asterisk <RequiredAsterisk />
				</Text>
			</FormHeader>
			<FormSection>
				{/* Example 1: Maximum characters only with default messages */}
```
